contexts.text: The sun waxed hot and it melted () = that it vanished according to the degree of the increasing concupiscence... To melt = to vanish.
The hills shall melt ()... As the love of self and of the world is meant, it is said melt... for fire = these loves; and to melt, and be burnt up, = to perish thereby. AE 741:21.
Concerning the evils of the loves of self and of the world, which are signified by the mountains, it is said that they shall melt like wax before the fire (); because fire = those loves.
Thou hast melted, O Philistia, the whole of thee () = the vastation of the Church as to the truth of doctrine, and thence as to faith. AE 817:9.
The heart of Egypt shall melt in the midst of it () = (the destruction of) the natural man separated from the spiritual. ( = the terror of the natural man on account of visitation. AE 654:48.)
